entries.subject: Temperature at 15 um from ten JWST MIRI visits
entries.finding: The lens. Ten MIRI/F1500W visits (program 3077's phase curve, 1177 observations 7-11, 2304 observations 1-4) reduced from raw on Bell's settings with a fractional-pixel aperture, fitted jointly with his model; the joint fit gives a dayside of 859 ppm against Bell's 797 +/- 77. The package orbit's 2015 osculating elements put the 2022 eclipses 2.0 to 2.4 h early; the lens uses the linear ephemeris of these observations (60271.25431 BMJD, 1.5108699 d), which places all five eclipses within 1.3 min and improves chi-squared per sample from 1.039 to 0.985. A bare rock (T cos(z)^(1/4), nothing at night; Cowan & Agol 2011, eq. 3) gives 575 K under the star, 565 to 586 K at one standard deviation, 865 ppm at eclipse against Greene's 861, at the 562 K limit of a black rock. A free smooth map fits no better (chi-squared 6796.6 vs 6803.0 with one parameter more, BIC 6903 vs 6900) and puts the hot spot 1.6 deg from noon: the earlier 28 deg west offset was the timing error. North-south structure is the model's.

entries.subject: NASA Eyes on Exoplanets artist's concept map as an illustration lens
entries.finding: Shown as the non-default Illustration lens, never as imagery: the map NASA's Eyes on Exoplanets app lists for TRAPPIST-1b (TRAPPIST-1_b.jpg), resized unchanged onto the sphere with its left edge at 0° longitude, so its longitudes are arbitrary. No image resolves this planet; nothing in the map was observed. NASA credits the app NASA/JPL-Caltech and calls each planet's look an artist's concept; the file itself carries no credit or date.
